author_direction: On 2026-10-16 Kirk LaSalle asked to resolve the uneven testing of Candidates A and B now ('Let's resolve this now'). He was asked to choose the precise C and M for Candidate A among three written options (1: M = all gravitating energy, an exact GR identity; 2: M = observed baryons with C = C_m, alpha = 1, a parameter-free falsification test; 3: option 2 plus a free exponent). He was unavailable and asked the assistant to choose pragmatically.
operationalization_note: Option 2 was chosen by the assistant because it is the only option that gives Candidate A an observational test without adding a departure from GR. It is not recorded as an author selection. If Kirk later selects a different meaning of C or M, this test remains the result for option 2 only and is not relabelled.
registration_scope: Local prospective numerical preregistration, frozen by SHA-256 before any computation with the decision statistic, nuisance treatments, comparator and thresholds defined here. It is not an external registry entry and it is not blind (see prior_knowledge_disclosure).
prior_knowledge_disclosure: Disc-galaxy rotation curves are known from decades of literature to exceed the Newtonian prediction of their observed baryons at large radii; McGaugh, Lelli and Schombert (2016) established the radial acceleration relation on this same SPARC sample. The direction of the outcome is therefore strongly expected.

This repository already computed the same mathematical model as option 2 under other nuisance treatments: docs/SHOW_YOUR_WORK.md section 4 reports 'Newtonian baryons only' chi2 = 605,258 against chi2 = 7,804 for baryons plus an isothermal halo on all 175 SPARC galaxies (Upsilon_disk fitted in [0.1, 2.0], no distance or inclination nuisance), and results/sparc_real_analysis.json reports a Newtonian baryons-only chi2 = 364,990 for the Q <= 2, inclination >= 30 degree sample with the Upsilon prior.

The SPARC Q <= 2 and Q = 3 samples were profiled for acceleration laws in results/real_data_v1/sparc_profile_validation.json and results/real_data_v1/sparc_q3_holdout_v1.json. Every galaxy used here has been examined before.
No computation using the T1/T2 nested-comparator statistic, the error-inflation rule or the thresholds below has been run before this freeze.

The value of this test is therefore not discovery. It is the formal application of a fixed rule to Candidate A's declared operationalization, with nuisance freedom deliberately chosen to favour Candidate A.

operationalization.C: C_m = (G_mu_nu + Lambda g_mu_nu) n^mu n^nu for the static observer n of each galaxy
operationalization.M: observed baryonic mass density rho_bar (stars and helium-corrected gas)
operationalization.relation: rho_bar = k (C_m / C0)^alpha with alpha = 1 and k = c^2 C0 / (8 pi G), i.e. rho_bar = c^2 C_m / (8 pi G)
operationalization.tidal_curvature: sqrt(K) is kept as a separate geometric diagnostic and is not a matter source
weak_field_reduction: For a weak, quasi-static field with |Phi| << c^2, speeds << c and pressure << rho c^2, Einstein's equation gives C_m = 8 pi G rho_dyn / c^2 = 2 laplacian(Phi_obs) / c^2, where Phi_obs is the potential traced by the observed dynamics.
Option 2 therefore states laplacian(Phi_obs) = 4 pi G rho_bar = laplacian(Phi_bar) everywhere. For an isolated galaxy with Phi -> 0 at infinity, Poisson uniqueness gives Phi_obs = Phi_bar.
The midplane circular speed then satisfies V_obs(R)^2 = V_bar(R)^2 at every radius, with V_bar^2 = V_gas|V_gas| + Upsilon_disk V_disk|V_disk| + Upsilon_bulge V_bul|V_bul| from the SPARC mass models.
The cosmological-constant term is negligible: |Lambda c^2| is about 1e-35 s^-2, about 1e-4 of 4 pi G rho in the outer discs of SPARC galaxies, and C_m removes the vacuum term by construction.

population.primary: SPARC quality flag Q <= 2, catalogue inclination >= 30 degrees, at least 3 points after the point filter (the certified load_sparc defaults)
population.primary_expected_counts: the certified pipeline reports 153 galaxies and 3168 points for this selection; any difference is reported as a deviation
population.secondary: Q = 3 with the same inclination and point rules; reported separately and never changes the primary outcome
population.error_treatment: observed velocity uncertainty floored at 1 km/s, as in the certified pipeline
population.exclusions: No galaxy satisfying the rules may be removed after any outcome is computed.

model.nuisance_parameters: x = (log10 Upsilon_disk, f_D, i) per galaxy, Upsilon_bulge = 1.4 Upsilon_disk
model.nuisance_bounds: log10 Upsilon_disk in [-1.3, 0.7]; f_D in [max(1 - 5 sigma_fD, 0.3), 1 + 5 sigma_fD]; i in [max(i0 - 5 sigma_i, 10), min(i0 + 5 sigma_i, 90)] degrees; sigma_fD = max(e_D / D, 0.02); sigma_i = max(e_i, 1 degree)
model.a2_prediction: V_A2 = sqrt(max(V_bar^2, 0.01 km^2 s^-2) * f_D) * sin(i) / sin(i0), identical to the certified pipeline residual with nu = 1
model.reference_comparator: REF adds a non-negative pseudo-isothermal unseen-mass term: V_REF = sqrt(max(V_bar^2, 0.01) * f_D + s * (1 - (r_c / R) arctan(R / r_c))) * sin(i) / sin(i0), with s in [0, 250000] (km/s)^2 and log10(r_c / kpc) in [-2, 2], R the catalogue radius. s = 0 recovers A2 exactly. The term can only add positive circular-speed support, so any improvement over A2 measures a need for unseen mass. REF is standard phenomenology used as a yardstick, not a claim about dark matter.

treatments.T1_certified_priors: Q = chi2 + ((log10 Upsilon_disk - log10 0.5) / 0.1)^2 + ((f_D - 1) / sigma_fD)^2 + ((i - i0) / sigma_i)^2
treatments.T2_generous_to_A: as T1 without the Upsilon_disk term, so Upsilon_disk is free from 0.05 to 5.0, far beyond usual maximum-disk values

fitting.optimizer: scipy.optimize.least_squares, method trf, 3-point finite-difference Jacobian, ftol = xtol = 1e-10, gtol = 1e-9, max_nfev = 2000
fitting.a2_starts: log10 Upsilon_disk in {log10 0.5, log10 0.5 - 0.3, log10 0.5 + 0.3, 0.69} crossed with (f_D, i) in {(1, i0), (1 + 2 sigma_fD, i0 + 2 sigma_i)}, clipped to the bounds
fitting.ref_starts: the best A2 nuisance values with s in {0.25, 1} x max(V_obs)^2 and log10 r_c in {log10 0.5, log10 2, log10 8}; plus each A2 Upsilon start at nominal (f_D, i) with s = max(V_obs)^2 and r_c = 2 kpc
fitting.nesting: Q_REF is the minimum of every converged REF start and Q_A2 (the s = 0 point), so Q_A2 - Q_REF >= 0 by construction
fitting.convergence: a start counts only if least_squares reports success with a finite cost; every galaxy, model and treatment cell needs at least one counted start

statistics.error_inflation: lambda = max(1, chi2_data(REF) summed over the population / max(N_points - 5 N_galaxies, 1)), computed separately per treatment; Delta_Q_i_cons = Delta_Q_i / lambda
statistics.population_threshold: the 0.999 quantile of chi2 with 2 N_galaxies degrees of freedom
statistics.galaxy_threshold: the 0.999 quantile of chi2 with 2 degrees of freedom (13.8155)
statistics.calibration_caveat: Thresholds are nominal. Under A2 the comparator sits on a boundary (s = 0) with r_c unidentified, radial covariance is unknown and the objective includes priors, so these are not calibrated significances.

outcome_rules.rejected: Delta_Q_cons exceeds the population threshold under both T1 and T2 for the primary population: the SPARC rotation curves require mass beyond observed baryons even with nuisance freedom favouring A, so Candidate A in its option 2 operationalization is falsified for disc galaxies
outcome_rules.not_rejected: Delta_Q_cons does not exceed the population threshold under T1 or under T2
outcome_rules.incomplete: a data hash mismatch, a cell without a counted start, or any non-finite value; stop and report

reported_descriptives: galaxy and point counts per population
lambda, Delta_Q_cons and thresholds per treatment
number and fraction of galaxies with Delta_Q_i_cons above the galaxy threshold and best REF s > 0
median and 16th/84th percentiles of the outermost-point ratio V_obs^2 / V_A2^2 at the A2 optimum per treatment
fraction of galaxies whose T2 Upsilon_disk optimum lies at the upper bound
sensitivity_never_the_result: T1 with Upsilon_disk prior centre 0.4 and 0.6
interpretation_limits: A rejection falsifies only option 2 (M = observed baryons, C = C_m, alpha = 1). Option 1 (M = all gravitating energy) is an exact GR identity and cannot be tested this way.
Calling the missing mass 'emergent matter' would be a relabelling unless Candidate A independently predicted its amount and distribution before seeing these data.
SPARC mass models assume disc thickness and circular orbits; non-circular motions, asymmetric drift and warps are not modelled.
A non-rejection would not confirm Candidate A; it would only mean this rule did not exclude it.
